title: Course section
description: Content model for the course's identity and catalog copy (_data/course.json, exposed as the `course` global). Several properties are elements Meredith College requires on every syllabus. Think before removing a property or loosening `required`. Property order here is the suggested authoring order.

$schema.description: Relative path to this schema, for editor validation.

code.description: Catalog code in display casing (e.g. CS101) — the course number Meredith requires on the syllabus. Slugs derive by lowercasing.

name.description: Course name as it appears in the catalog — the course name Meredith requires on the syllabus. NOT `title`: page titles ("CODE: Name (Term)") are computed by the kit.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the section; drives listing copy.

term.description: The term this section runs in. Must name an entry in _data/dates.json (year, then season), so a new term is one edit here plus the calendar.

description.description: Catalog description, verbatim — Meredith requires the catalog description on the syllabus, so do not editorialize here; section-specific prose belongs in `approach`.

approach.description: Optional section-specific framing of how THIS section runs the course; the catalog `description` stays untouched.

prerequisiteNote.description: Qualifier appended to the prerequisite list, e.g. the grade floor: "with a grade of C or better".

outcomes.description: The committed catalog outcomes, verbatim — the course objectives and expected learning outcomes Meredith requires, each stating what students will know and be able to do. Section extras go in `additionalOutcomes`.

additionalOutcomes.description: Section-specific outcomes layered on top of the committed catalog set.

textbook.description: Required text and how to get it — the textbook/materials element Meredith requires. Omit the whole key ONLY when the course has no text: the `<syllabus>` component then renders "No text is required.", which is still an explicit materials statement. Never leave the key present but empty.

required.description: The required text, including cost/format notes (e.g. "free, online").

requirements.description: Non-textbook requirements: software, hardware, accounts. Meredith requires a statement about required access to technology; the `<syllabus>` component always prints the laptop sentence and appends these, so list every tool students must install or sign up for (or say explicitly that nothing beyond the laptop is needed).

documents.description: Course-wide documents (syllabus PDF, project specs, policies) shown on the landing page; per-week material belongs in that week's `resources`.

href.description: Absolute URL for external material, or site-relative path (e.g. /resources/…) for published files.
